newsitem.title: UK: Sun Co to save on fleet sale to Maritrans.
newsitem.headline: Sun Co to save on fleet sale to Maritrans.

text.p: Sun Co Inc's Sun Transport said Tuesday it expected savings from the disposal of its remaining shipping fleet to Maritrans Inc for $30 million.
A Sun spokesman said: "We expect to see some savings from getting out of the maritime business and instead buying in those specialist services."
He added: "What we need is for our petroleum products to be moved. We do not need to be the mover."
"We were not big enough to be efficient and were something of a high cost operator."
Maritrans chairman and chief executive Stephen Van Dyck said: "We have not completed the purchase yet, but we have entered into a binding agreement to acquire the vessels."
Maritrans is to acquire the 34,000 dwt petroleum product tankers Philadelphia Sun and New York Sun and two tug/oil products barge combinations.
Sun said it had agreed long-term contracts for the future operation of the assets being sold.
The two tug/barge combinations will continue to operate between Sun's Puerto Rico refinery and other parts of the island.
The Philadelphia Sun will operate between the Puerto Rico refinery and Sun's Marcus Hook, Pa., facility, while the New York Sun will remain on charter to the U.S. Military Sealift Command, Sun said.

Van Dyck said the acquisition fitted with Maritrans strategy. "Our long-term strategy has been, and continues to be, to gain contracts of affreightment for oil products in the Gulf of Mexico and on the East Coast of the U.S.," he said.
Maritrans is not actively pursuing any other acquisitions at present, Van Dyck added.
"We are always looking around with our eyes open, but there are no specific deals under discussion at present. There will be a lot of work to integrate the Sun vessels."
In June, Sun Transport sold its 3,550 dwt tanker Eastern Sun to John W. Stone, and four tug/barge combinations to LeeVac Corp. Terms for either deal were not disclosed.
